name: Tephra Geochemical Correlation
mechanism: Compare measured glass or mineral composition and stratigraphic context to correlate attributable volcanic ash layers between sites.
operating_requirement: Collect actual ash samples, separate and inspect components, pay calibrated compositional analyses and reference access, and retain contamination and competing matches.
consequence: Supply a supported layer-correlation record to regional geological and hazard reconstruction; an age transfers only from an independently dated, defensible match.
semantic_boundary: Petrography identifies constituents; this compares source fingerprints across retained layers. Similar bulk chemistry alone cannot establish a unique eruption or numerical date.
implementation_acceptance: Mix two source layers and require an ambiguous result rather than silently selecting a reference; removing the dated reference removes numerical age transfer.
branching_note: All named foundations apply. Instruments, samples and reference services remain separate paid physical requirements; knowledge does not create equipment or evidence.
recovery: Acquire attributable method instruction, samples or specialist service through a reachable competent partner, then fund a local qualification.

name: Fossil Biostratigraphic Correlation
mechanism: Use identified fossil assemblages and their observed stratigraphic ranges to compare the relative positions of sedimentary sections.
operating_requirement: Pay measured section sampling, specimen preparation, taxonomic comparison and specialist interpretation against attributable regional reference ranges.
consequence: Constrain relative correlations for mapping and geological reconstruction; regional absences, reworked fossils and barren intervals remain explicit limits.
semantic_boundary: Layer order and organism classification do not themselves correlate distant strata. Fossil similarity supports a contextual relative correlation, not an automatic absolute age.
implementation_acceptance: Place a reworked older fossil above a younger assemblage and require review of the conflicting evidence; a barren interval must not acquire an invented zone.
branching_note: All named foundations apply. Instruments, samples and reference services remain separate paid physical requirements; knowledge does not create equipment or evidence.
recovery: Acquire attributable method instruction, samples or specialist service through a reachable competent partner, then fund a local qualification.

name: Speleothem Uranium-Series Chronology
mechanism: Infer cave-carbonate formation timing from measured uranium-series disequilibrium with explicit initial-contamination and closed-system assumptions.
operating_requirement: Use attributable sampled carbonate, paid clean preparation and isotope measurements, blanks and standards, replicate layers and a stated detrital correction model.
consequence: Provide qualified sample ages and uncertainties for cave-water or environmental histories; disturbed or contaminated material can remain undated.
semantic_boundary: This interprets carbonate disequilibrium rather than radiocarbon calibration or generic decay arithmetic. A date on one sampled layer does not date an entire cave.
implementation_acceptance: Vary the assumed initial thorium contribution and retain the resulting uncertainty; a failed replicate or open-system flag blocks a precise accepted age.
branching_note: All named foundations apply. Instruments, samples and reference services remain separate paid physical requirements; knowledge does not create equipment or evidence.
recovery: Acquire attributable method instruction, samples or specialist service through a reachable competent partner, then fund a local qualification.

name: Helium-Retention Thermochronology
mechanism: Interpret measured radiogenic helium and parent-element content in identified mineral grains through a stated helium-retention and thermal-history model.
operating_requirement: Pay grain selection and geometry measurement, controlled gas extraction, helium and parent assays, blanks, references and comparison of candidate cooling histories.
consequence: Constrain possible cooling or reheating histories of sampled minerals; report nonunique histories and grain-dependent behavior rather than a universal crystallization date.
semantic_boundary: Helium loss and retention constrain thermal history differently from fission-track annealing or argon release spectra; none replaces the others as a universal clock.
implementation_acceptance: Compare distinct cooling paths compatible with the observations and retain their ambiguity; changing the grain-retention assumptions must affect the supported history.

name: Fluid-Inclusion Microthermometry
mechanism: Observe phase changes in qualified trapped-fluid inclusions during calibrated heating and cooling to constrain fluid properties under stated models.
operating_requirement: Prepare suitable retained mineral sections, inspect inclusion integrity, pay a calibrated microscope heating/cooling stage and repeated observations, and preserve calibration and phase-identification uncertainty.
consequence: Supply temperature and composition constraints to mineral-deposit or hydrothermal interpretation; homogenization temperature alone does not establish an unconditional trapping temperature.
semantic_boundary: Microscopic inclusion phase behavior differs from measuring a rock's present bulk temperature or its crystallization age. Altered inclusions and ambiguous phase changes remain invalid or unresolved.
implementation_acceptance: A damaged inclusion cannot produce a qualified result; changing the pressure or composition assumptions must preserve the corresponding interpretive limitation.

recovery: Acquire attributable method instruction, samples or specialist service through a reachable competent partner, then fund a local qualification.

name: Carbonate Clumped-Isotope Thermometry
mechanism: Compare measured heavy-isotope association in carbonate with attributable calibration to constrain formation or resetting temperature under a declared model.
operating_requirement: Pay retained carbonate sampling, controlled preparation, suitable isotope-ratio measurement, standards and corrections; assess disequilibrium and later alteration before interpretation.
consequence: Provide qualified paleotemperature constraints for environmental or burial-history analysis with uncertainties and unresolved alternative explanations.
semantic_boundary: Bulk isotope ratios and ordinary thermometry do not measure isotope association. Solution chemistry and subsequent alteration can prevent a unique formation-temperature interpretation.
implementation_acceptance: A calibration failure blocks temperature release, and a disequilibrium or recrystallization flag prevents the result being labeled an unqualified formation temperature.
branching_note: All named foundations apply. Instruments, samples and reference services remain separate paid physical requirements; knowledge does not create equipment or evidence.
recovery: Acquire attributable method instruction, samples or specialist service through a reachable competent partner, then fund a local qualification.
